svg.title: PEM electrolyzer stack, assembled and exploded isometric view
svg.desc: A proton-exchange-membrane electrolyzer cell, shown clamped (plates flush on the membrane, tie rods inside the stack, nuts tight on the top end plate) and pulled apart along four tie rods at one even spacing, with dashed axes running port to port through three manifolds: the bottom end plate with the water inlet feeding the water manifold, a bipolar plate whose pixel serpentine flow field runs from the water port to the oxygen-and-water port through short feed channels, while the hydrogen port is sealed off by its own O-ring, the membrane electrode assembly, a second bipolar plate, and the top end plate carrying the oxygen outlet on the anode manifold and the hydrogen outlet on the cathode manifold, where bubbles rise at a two-to-one hydrogen-to-oxygen ratio.
